title: Paul Verlaine's birth chart
metaDescription: Paul Verlaine's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.9° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Aries — the Sun, Mercury, Uranus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aries, but precisely: 9.9°, first decan, 0°–10°, under Mars in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aries (1.1°), Venus in Taurus (20.6°), Mars in Taurus (18.3°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste for the substantial and the lasting, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Neptune and Pluto: 0.7° from an exact sextile. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Mars sextile Jupiter at 0.9°, and Mercury conjunction Uranus at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has five entries for this chart. The Sun in Aries at 9.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Taurus at 20.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Taurus at 18.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Pisces at 17.4° is in domicile; Saturn in Aquarius at 5.5° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 fire, 2 earth, 2 air, 1 water; by modality, 5 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable. All ten bodies ran direct that day — a chart with no apparent reversals anywhere in it.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.6° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 18.9°.
